title: Left scalar-homogeneity of the symplectic form
statement:
Let $p$ be prime and work over the prime field $\bbf_p$, with $V = \bbf_p^n \times \bbf_p^n$ carrying the symplectic form $\omega$ given by $\omega(u,v) = \sum_{i=0}^{n-1}(x_i z'_i - z_i x'_i)$ for $u=(x,z)$ and $v=(x',z')$. Then for every scalar $c \in \bbf_p$ and all $x, y \in V$,
\[
\omega(c\,x,\, y) \;=\; c\,\omega(x, y),
\]
where $c\,x$ denotes the coordinatewise scalar multiplication of $x$ by $c$.
hypotheses_covered: p prime, working over the field F_p
V = F_p^n × F_p^n with the symplectic form ω
replaced:
Let $p$ be prime and work over the space $V = \bbf_p^n \times \bbf_p^n$ equipped with
the symplectic form $\omega(u,v) = \sum_{i=0}^{n-1}(x_i z'_i - z_i x'_i)$, where $u =
(x,z)$ and $v = (x',z')$. Then for all $x, y, z \in V$,
\[
\omega(x + y, z) = \omega(x, z) + \omega(y, z).
\]
